extraction.name: AI2 Reasoning Challenge (ARC)
extraction.description: A question set, text corpus, and baselines assembled to encourage AI research in advanced question answering.
extraction.creator: Peter Clark, Isaac Cowhey, Oren Etzioni, Tushar Khot, Ashish Sabharwal, Carissa Schoenick, Oyvind Tafjord
extraction.rai:dataCollection: The ARC dataset consists of 7787 science questions, all non-diagram, multiple choice (typically 4-way multiple choice). They are drawn from a variety of sources, and sorted into a Challenge Set of 2590 “hard” questions (those that both a retrieval and a co-occurrence method fail to answer correctly) and an Easy Set of 5197 questions.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: The questions were drawn from a variety of sources, including standardized tests such as ACTAAP, AIMS, Alaska Dept Ed, AMP, CA Stnds Test, FCAT, LA Ed Assm. Prog, MD School Assm., MCAS, MEA, MEAP, Mercury, MSA, NAEP, NC READY, NY Regents, Ohio Achieve. Tests, TAKS, TIMSS, V A Stds of Leaming, WASL.
extraction.rai:dataSocialImpact: The dataset is designed to encourage research on questions requiring reasoning, use of commonsense knowledge, or other advanced methods for deeper text comprehension.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: The dataset has two potentially significant challenges. First, these datasets are often small (e.g., hundreds of questions), due to the scarcity of public, real-world test data. Second, because tests were designed for people rather than machines, large portions of these tests can be easily solved by simple AI methods.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: The dataset can be used for Training, Testing, Validation, Fine Tuning. The usage guidelines are that systems are not restricted to the provided corpus, but use of the corpus is optional.
